html:
The Belizean and Guatemalan territorial dispute is Guatemala's long claim to all or part of Belize. Guatemala wrote it into its constitution in 1945 and did not recognise Belize until 1991.

Guatemala says it inherited Spain's rights to the land and that the 1859 border treaty with Britain lapsed when Britain failed to build a promised road. Britain held that British Honduras was lawfully British. The threat of invasion delayed independence until 1981, and British troops stayed to defend Belize until 1994.

In referendums in 2018 and 2019, voters in both countries agreed to send the dispute to the International Court of Justice. The claim is one of the oldest open border quarrels in the Americas, with roots in the treaties of the 1700s and in Guatemala's national story.
sum: The Belizean and Guatemalan territorial dispute is Guatemala's long claim to all or part of Belize. Guatemala wrote it into its constitution in 1945 and did not recognise Belize until 1991.
